labels.note: The Supabase client is built from process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (line 4) and exported (createClient at line 6). The service_role key bypasses all Row Level Security, and the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix makes Next.js inline its value into the client bundle; this module is imported by the client component components/PurchaseCredits.tsx (import at line 2), so the full-admin key ships to every visitor's browser and grants unrestricted read/write to the whole database.

notes: Provenance: whoiskatrin/chart-gpt, a real, popular public Next.js (pages-router) app -- ChartGPT, chart generation from text -- (recall case; NOT authored by us). The single, unambiguous issue is a service_role key exposed to the browser: lib/supabase.tsx reads NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (also declared in .env.example line 4) and the resulting admin client is imported into a React client component (components/PurchaseCredits.tsx) as well as server helpers (utils/helper.ts). Because service_role bypasses RLS, exposing it client-side is a critical privilege escalation for any visitor. Deliberate non-findings: .env.example ships only empty placeholders (no committed secret value), so this is privileged-key-client, not exposed-secret; the anon key var (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, .env.example line 3) is public by design and not flagged. MANIFEST TRIMMED (0.3.1, ERR-007): repo/package.json keeps only the dependencies project_model.mjs can read (see bench/wild/observable-packages.mjs), at their real upstream versions -- the rest were deleted because they are invisible to every engine pass and each one raised a Dependabot alert against a fixture that is never installed. No version was changed, and no label here is a dependency label, so nothing this case measures moves.
